message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** | Alfred Hitchcock | The masterclass of suspense and the iconic shower scene. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | A chilling psychological descent set in an isolated hotel. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | A tense, atmospheric paranoia thriller with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** | M. Night Shyamalan | A twist‑filled supernatural mystery that redefined the genre. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | A fast‑paced, post‑apocalyptic horror that revitalized the zombie sub‑genre. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan | The start of a gritty, puzzle‑based horror franchise that’s still popular. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found‑footage film that made audiences jump out of their seats. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | A well‑crafted haunted‑house story that spawned a whole universe of films. |
| 2013 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | A fresh take on the supernatural with a relentless, creeping dread. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | A slow‑burning, atmospheric horror rooted in Puritan folklore. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | A smart social satire wrapped in a terrifying thriller. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | John Krasinski | A tense, sound‑driven horror that keeps you on edge. |
| 2020 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | A daylight horror that turns a festival into a nightmare. |
| 2021 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling of the classic with a strong female lead. |
| 2022 | **Evil Dead Rise** | Lee Cronin | A fresh, brutal take on the cult‑classic franchise. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | Gerard Johnstone | A creepy, AI‑powered horror that taps into our tech anxieties. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or found‑footage—and enjoy the chills!
